notes.1: Reduces the style to a text terminal. It drops the rule that every image is glyphs chosen by ink density on a grid whose scale is the only camera. Its 'one hue, light only means the phosphor is lit, no green' rule bans the original's green/white phosphors and its one warm surprise.
notes.2: Warm near-black glass, bloom and scanlines are right, but it forbids the original's glass (slight barrel curvature, rounded mask, fine noise) and prescribes smooth vector mono where the original uses a bitmap-style terminal face (VT323). No afterglow, flicker or phosphor luminance ramp.
notes.3: One phosphor with a dim/normal/bold ramp and inverse video is right, but 'never introduce a second hue' contradicts the original's one soft second colour reserved for the emotional object. Amber is fixed where the original allows green or white.
notes.4: LOG-strip subtitles under a rule, typed titles and the hold rule match. The inverse-video tag only appears in §8.
notes.5: Constant-rate grid typing and the eased grid push are right. But status words 'stamp in' with an off-grid scale and fade, where the original keeps glyphs on the grid outside declared transformations. Typing as performance (even machine vs uneven human) is reduced to one constant rate.
notes.6: Locked screen, push to the title, and clear/power as on-screen transitions match. Pull-out, scroll, push into a glyph and text-becomes-image are absent but unshown.
notes.8: Log file, promote-to-title, power-off and cursor moves match. Picture-made-of-words is absent (unshown); the single colour change is excluded by §3.
notes.9: No overlap with the original's pitfalls, which are about glyph pictures and engine traps (unshown), but nothing here contradicts the style.
notes.10: Covers typing on a grid, grid zoom, power on/off, bloom and scanlines. No density ramp or curved-glass phosphor post.
notes.11: Structures, openings and endings fit the style, but '§3 fixes the palette' closes choices the original leaves open (the phosphor colour, and whether the second colour appears at all).
